### Pattern 34 — JaCoCo for Java: line, branch, and instruction coverage in Maven/Gradle projects  [official]

JaCoCo (Java Code Coverage) is the standard coverage tool for JVM projects. It operates at
the bytecode level (like Pitest) and supports four coverage metrics not available in most
JavaScript tools: **instruction**, **line**, **branch**, and **complexity** coverage.
For polyglot teams maintaining both TypeScript and Java services, understanding JaCoCo's
configuration prevents "why does Java coverage look different?" confusion.

JaCoCo's **instruction** coverage is finer than line coverage: a single Java source line
can produce multiple bytecode instructions, and JaCoCo tracks each one. This gives more
granular data than Istanbul's line counting. JaCoCo's **complexity** metric counts cyclomatic
complexity paths — a proxy for the number of test cases needed to achieve full branch coverage.

```xml
<!-- pom.xml — JaCoCo Maven plugin: enforce branch thresholds on CI -->
<build>
  <plugins>
    <plugin>
      <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
      <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
      <version>0.8.12</version>
      <executions>
        <!-- Instrument bytecode before tests run -->
        <execution>
          <id>prepare-agent</id>
          <goals><goal>prepare-agent</goal></goals>
        </execution>
        <!-- Generate HTML + XML reports after tests complete -->
        <execution>
          <id>report</id>
          <phase>test</phase>
          <goals><goal>report</goal></goals>
        </execution>
        <!-- CI gate: fail if thresholds are breached -->
        <execution>
          <id>jacoco-check</id>
          <goals><goal>check</goal></goals>
          <configuration>
            <rules>
              <rule>
                <element>BUNDLE</element>
                <limits>
                  <!-- Global branch coverage floor — fail below 75% -->
                  <limit>
                    <counter>BRANCH</counter>
                    <value>COVEREDRATIO</value>
                    <minimum>0.75</minimum>
                  </limit>
                  <!-- Global line coverage floor -->
                  <limit>
                    <counter>LINE</counter>
                    <value>COVEREDRATIO</value>
                    <minimum>0.80</minimum>
                  </limit>
                </limits>
              </rule>
              <!-- Per-class threshold for payment package -->
              <rule>
                <element>CLASS</element>
                <includes>
                  <include>com/example/payments/**</include>
                </includes>
                <limits>
                  <limit>
                    <counter>BRANCH</counter>
                    <value>COVEREDRATIO</value>
                    <minimum>0.90</minimum>
                  </limit>
                </limits>
              </rule>
            </rules>
          </configuration>
        </execution>
      </executions>
    </plugin>
  </plugins>
</build>
```

```bash
# Run tests with JaCoCo coverage and enforce thresholds (Maven):
mvn test jacoco:check

# Generate HTML report only (no threshold check):
mvn test jacoco:report

# Exclude generated JAXB/Lombok files from coverage — add to jacoco-maven-plugin <configuration>:
# <excludes>
#   <exclude>**/generated/**/*.class</exclude>
#   <exclude>**/*Lombok*.class</exclude>
# </excludes>
```

**Tradeoff**: JaCoCo bytecode instrumentation adds ~10 % test overhead and requires the JVM
agent on the classpath. Use JaCoCo for compliance artefacts and PR gates; use Pitest for
mutation-based quality signals. Do NOT use JaCoCo to measure Kotlin code compiled with
`data class` — Kotlin's compiler-generated `equals`/`hashCode`/`copy` methods inflate
uncovered branch counts the same way TypeScript decorators do in Istanbul (see G63 below).

### Pattern 35 — coverage.py with pytest-cov: branch coverage gates for Python services  [official]

Python's `coverage.py` (via `pytest-cov`) is the canonical Python coverage tool. Unlike
Istanbul, which instruments the JavaScript AST, `coverage.py` hooks into Python's trace
function at the interpreter level. Branch tracking is opt-in (`--branch`) and Python's
`else` clause on `for`/`while` loops counts as a branch — an unusual construct that
surprises JavaScript developers joining Python codebases.

```python
# pyproject.toml — pytest + coverage.py configuration for Python services
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--cov=src --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=lcov:coverage.lcov --cov-fail-under=80"
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true          # enable branch coverage (default: False — line only)
source = ["src"]
omit = [
    "src/**/__init__.py",   # empty init files
    "src/**/migrations/**", # Django/Alembic generated files
    "src/**/proto/**",      # generated protobuf stubs
    "*/site-packages/*",    # third-party libraries
]
relative_files = true  # store relative paths in .coverage — portability across CI

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true     # show uncovered line numbers in terminal
skip_covered = false    # do NOT skip fully-covered files by default
fail_under = 80         # exit code 2 if coverage < 80%
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",      # equivalent of /* istanbul ignore next */
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",     # type-only imports: never run at runtime
    "raise NotImplementedError",  # abstract method stubs
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",   # abstract method decorators
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:", # script entry points
]
```

```python
# src/utils/pricing.py — example showing for/else branch coverage Python tracks
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Optional

TIER_DISCOUNTS = {
    'premium': Decimal('0.20'),
    'standard': Decimal('0.10'),
    'basic': Decimal('0.00'),
}

def apply_tier_discount(price: Decimal, user_tier: str) -> Optional[Decimal]:
    """Return discounted price or None if tier is unknown."""
    for tier, discount in TIER_DISCOUNTS.items():
        if tier == user_tier:
            return price * (1 - discount)
    else:
        # Python for/else: the `else` branch runs when the loop completes WITHOUT a break.
        # coverage.py tracks this as a separate branch — Istanbul has no equivalent.
        return None
```

```python
# tests/test_pricing.py — must exercise the for/else branch to satisfy coverage.py
from decimal import Decimal
from src.utils.pricing import apply_tier_discount

def test_premium_discount():
    assert apply_tier_discount(Decimal('100.00'), 'premium') == Decimal('80.00')

def test_standard_discount():
    assert apply_tier_discount(Decimal('100.00'), 'standard') == Decimal('90.00')

def test_unknown_tier_returns_none():
    # This test exercises the for/else branch — without it, coverage.py
    # reports a missing branch on the for statement's else path.
    assert apply_tier_discount(Decimal('100.00'), 'enterprise') is None
```

```bash
# Run with branch coverage and fail-under gate:
pytest --cov=src --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=80

# Generate HTML report for branch gap analysis:
pytest --cov=src --cov-branch --cov-report=html:htmlcov

# Generate LCOV for Codecov or SonarCloud upload:
pytest --cov=src --cov-branch --cov-report=lcov:coverage.lcov
```

**Tradeoff**: `coverage.py` branch tracking counts Python `for`/`while` `else` clauses and
implicit `raise`/`return` exits as branches. These are often genuinely worth testing (the
"loop completed without finding a match" path is a valid edge case) but can surprise developers
from JavaScript backgrounds. Add `exclude_lines` patterns for abstract methods and
`if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks to avoid phantom uncovered-line noise from type-only code. Do NOT
use `branch = false` (the default) in CI — line-only coverage misses the most common real-world
Python bug pattern: missing `else` on a conditional that should have a fallback.

### Pattern 36 — SonarCloud / SonarQube LCOV import: unified coverage dashboard across TypeScript and Python  [official]

SonarCloud and SonarQube accept LCOV-format coverage reports from any language tool (Jest,
Vitest, coverage.py, JaCoCo) and aggregate them into a single quality dashboard. For teams
maintaining mixed TypeScript + Python services, a unified Sonar dashboard provides
cross-service coverage trends combined with static analysis and security signals.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/sonar.yml — combined TypeScript + Python coverage upload to SonarCloud
name: Sonar Coverage

on: [pull_request, push]

jobs:
  coverage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0    # required for SonarCloud blame tracking

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22' }

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.12' }

      - name: Install TypeScript deps
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run TypeScript tests with LCOV coverage
        run: npx vitest run --coverage --coverage.reporter=lcov
        # Produces: coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Install Python deps
        run: pip install pytest pytest-cov

      - name: Run Python tests with LCOV coverage
        run: pytest --cov=src --cov-branch --cov-report=lcov:python-coverage.lcov

      - name: Run SonarCloud analysis
        uses: SonarSource/sonarcloud-github-action@master
        env:
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
        with:
          args: >
            -Dsonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths=coverage/lcov.info
            -Dsonar.python.coverage.reportPaths=python-coverage.lcov
            -Dsonar.coverage.exclusions=**/generated/**,**/__mocks__/**,**/migrations/**
```

```properties
# sonar-project.properties — SonarCloud project configuration
sonar.projectKey=my-org_my-repo
sonar.organization=my-org
sonar.sources=src,python/src
sonar.tests=src,python/tests
sonar.test.inclusions=**/*.test.ts,**/*.spec.ts,**/test_*.py,**/*_test.py
sonar.coverage.exclusions=**/generated/**,**/__mocks__/**,**/migrations/**,**/*.d.ts
sonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths=coverage/lcov.info
sonar.python.coverage.reportPaths=python-coverage.lcov
```

**Tradeoff**: SonarCloud provides rich trend dashboards and combines coverage with security (SAST),
duplication, and maintainability metrics. The downside: LCOV files must be generated before the
Sonar scan runs — if tests fail, no coverage data is uploaded. Set `reportOnFailure: true` in Vitest
config (Pattern 28) so LCOV is always written. Do NOT use Sonar as the sole coverage gate — Sonar
quality gate latency (30–90 seconds) is unsuitable for fast PR feedback. Keep local Jest/Vitest
threshold checks for immediate feedback; use Sonar for trend analysis and org-level gate blocking.

### Pattern 37 — `c8` merge mode: combining V8 coverage across multiple Node.js processes  [official]

`c8` (the V8 coverage CLI tool) supports a merge mode for combining coverage data from
multiple independently spawned Node.js processes — useful for services that spawn worker
processes or run tests across multiple processes. Without merging, only the primary process's
coverage is captured.

```typescript
// src/workers/image-processor.ts — CPU-bound worker module
import { workerData, parentPort } from 'node:worker_threads';

export interface ImageTask {
  path: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}

export function processImage(task: ImageTask): { resized: boolean; path: string } {
  if (task.width <= 0 || task.height <= 0) {
    throw new RangeError(`Invalid dimensions: ${task.width}x${task.height}`);
  }
  const resized = task.width > 0 && task.height > 0;
  return { resized, path: task.path };
}

if (workerData) {
  const result = processImage(workerData as ImageTask);
  parentPort?.postMessage(result);
}
```

```typescript
// tests/image-processor.test.ts — direct unit tests (in-process, covered by Vitest)
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { processImage } from '../src/workers/image-processor';

describe('processImage', () => {
  it('returns resized result for valid dimensions', () => {
    const result = processImage({ path: '/img/photo.jpg', width: 800, height: 600 });
    expect(result.resized).toBe(true);
    expect(result.path).toBe('/img/photo.jpg');
  });

  it('throws RangeError for zero width', () => {
    expect(() => processImage({ path: '/img/photo.jpg', width: 0, height: 600 }))
      .toThrow(RangeError);
  });

  it('throws RangeError for negative height', () => {
    expect(() => processImage({ path: '/img/photo.jpg', width: 100, height: -1 }))
      .toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});
```

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "test:coverage": "c8 --reporter=text --reporter=lcov --include='src/**/*.ts' --all vitest run",
    "test:coverage:workers": "NODE_V8_COVERAGE=./coverage-v8-unit node --experimental-strip-types --test src/**/*.test.ts && c8 report --reporter=text --reporter=lcov --temp-directory=./coverage-v8-unit"
  }
}
```

**Tradeoff**: `c8` merge mode is the correct approach for Node.js services using `cluster`,
`fork`, or `worker_threads` where Vitest's built-in V8 coverage misses worker-thread execution
paths. Use this pattern for Vitest 4.x projects — Vitest 5.0 adds native worker_threads coverage
tracking (G42), making manual `c8` merge unnecessary after upgrading. Do NOT mix `c8` V8 merge
mode with Istanbul-instrumented code — the two data formats are incompatible.

### Pattern 38 — Stryker mutation operator selection: targeted mutator configuration for TypeScript  [official]

Stryker applies mutation operators from a predefined set. The default set includes all operators,
which generates noise on configuration files, string literals, and arithmetic-heavy modules.
Selecting a targeted subset reduces mutation count, speeds CI, and focuses surviving mutant
reports on operators most likely to represent real bugs.

```typescript
// stryker.config.ts — targeted mutator selection for business logic modules
import type { PartialStrykerOptions } from '@stryker-mutator/api/core';

const config: PartialStrykerOptions = {
  testRunner: 'vitest',
  vitest: { configFile: 'vitest.config.ts' },
  coverageAnalysis: 'perTest',
  checkers: ['typescript'],
  tsconfigFile: 'tsconfig.json',

  mutate: [
    'src/domain/**/*.ts',
    'src/payments/**/*.ts',
    '!src/**/*.test.ts',
    '!src/**/__mocks__/**',
  ],

  // Full list: https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/mutation-testing-elements/supported-mutators/
  mutator: {
    excludedMutations: [
      // StringLiteral: noisy on i18n keys and log messages — rarely catches real bugs.
      'StringLiteral',
      // Regex: rarely produces meaningful surviving mutants in business logic.
      'Regex',
      // ObjectLiteral: mutating object keys rarely represents a real bug pattern.
      'ObjectLiteral',
    ],
  },

  thresholds: { high: 80, low: 60, break: 50 },
  reporters: ['html', 'progress', 'json'],
  timeoutMS: 5000,
  concurrency: 4,
  ignoreStatic: true,
  incremental: true,
  incrementalFile: '.stryker-tmp/incremental.json',
};

export default config;
```

```typescript
// stryker.fast.config.ts — only highest-signal mutators for a fast PR quality gate
import type { PartialStrykerOptions } from '@stryker-mutator/api/core';

const fastConfig: PartialStrykerOptions = {
  testRunner: 'vitest',
  vitest: { configFile: 'vitest.config.ts' },
  coverageAnalysis: 'perTest',
  checkers: ['typescript'],
  tsconfigFile: 'tsconfig.json',
  mutate: ['src/payments/**/*.ts', '!src/payments/**/*.test.ts'],
  mutator: {
    // Only highest-signal mutators for payment logic — reduces mutant count ~60%:
    includedMutations: [
      'ConditionalExpression',  // flips true/false in conditionals
      'EqualityOperator',       // changes === to !== — most common real bug
      'LogicalOperator',        // flips && to || — boolean logic errors
      'ArithmeticOperator',     // flips +/- and */÷ — critical for price calculations
    ],
  },
  thresholds: { high: 75, low: 55, break: 45 },
  reporters: ['progress', 'json'],
  timeoutMS: 3000,
  concurrency: '50%',
  incremental: true,
  incrementalFile: '.stryker-tmp/payments-incremental.json',
};

export default fastConfig;
```

**Tradeoff**: excluding `StringLiteral` and `Regex` reduces total mutant count by 15–30 % on
most TypeScript codebases, speeding CI and reducing false-positive surviving mutant noise. Do NOT
exclude `EqualityOperator` or `ConditionalExpression` from business logic modules — these represent
the highest-risk real-world bug pattern (off-by-one, wrong comparison operator) and should always
be tested. Reserve `includedMutations` fast-gate configs for PR pipelines; run the full operator
set in nightly runs to maintain comprehensive mutation coverage.

### Pattern 39 — Optional chaining and nullish coalescing: branch coverage completeness in TypeScript  [community]

TypeScript's `?.` (optional chaining) and `??` (nullish coalescing) operators each produce
two branches: the null/undefined path and the defined path. Istanbul instruments both; V8 in
Vitest < 3.2 often missed them. This pattern shows how to write tests that explicitly exercise
both branches of optional chaining to prevent phantom branch gaps.

```typescript
// src/domain/order-summary.ts
export interface OrderItem {
  sku: string;
  quantity: number;
  discount?: { code: string; percent: number };
}

export interface Customer {
  id: string;
  loyaltyPoints?: number;
  address?: { city: string; country: string };
}

export function buildOrderSummary(
  items: OrderItem[],
  customer: Customer,
): { itemCount: number; hasDiscount: boolean; loyaltyPoints: number; shippingCity: string; country: string } {
  // Each ?. and ?? creates an Istanbul branch — must test both paths.
  const loyaltyPoints = customer.loyaltyPoints ?? 0;        // branch: defined / undefined
  const shippingCity = customer.address?.city ?? 'Unknown'; // branch: defined / undefined (×2)
  const country = customer.address?.country ?? 'US';        // branch: defined / undefined (×2)
  const hasDiscount = items.some((item) => item.discount != null);
  return { itemCount: items.length, hasDiscount, loyaltyPoints, shippingCity, country };
}
```

```typescript
// src/domain/order-summary.test.ts — exhaustive branch coverage for ?. and ??
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { buildOrderSummary, type OrderItem, type Customer } from './order-summary';

const baseItem: OrderItem = { sku: 'SKU-1', quantity: 2 };
const discountItem: OrderItem = { sku: 'SKU-2', quantity: 1, discount: { code: 'SAVE10', percent: 10 } };

describe('buildOrderSummary — optional chaining branch coverage', () => {
  it('uses defaults when loyalty points and address are absent (undefined branches)', () => {
    const result = buildOrderSummary([baseItem], { id: 'c1' });
    expect(result.loyaltyPoints).toBe(0);          // ?? 0: undefined path
    expect(result.shippingCity).toBe('Unknown');   // ?.city ?? 'Unknown': address undefined
    expect(result.country).toBe('US');             // ?.country ?? 'US': address undefined
    expect(result.hasDiscount).toBe(false);
  });

  it('uses real values when loyalty points and address are present (defined branches)', () => {
    const customer: Customer = { id: 'c2', loyaltyPoints: 150, address: { city: 'Berlin', country: 'DE' } };
    const result = buildOrderSummary([baseItem], customer);
    expect(result.loyaltyPoints).toBe(150);        // ?? 0: defined path
    expect(result.shippingCity).toBe('Berlin');    // ?.city: defined path
    expect(result.country).toBe('DE');             // ?.country: defined path
  });

  it('detects discount when at least one item has a discount code', () => {
    const result = buildOrderSummary([baseItem, discountItem], { id: 'c3' });
    expect(result.hasDiscount).toBe(true);
  });

  it('reports no discount when no items have discount codes', () => {
    const result = buildOrderSummary([baseItem], { id: 'c4' });
    expect(result.hasDiscount).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff**: explicitly testing both the defined and undefined branch of every `?.` and `??`
is verbose but necessary for achieving meaningful branch coverage in TypeScript domain models.
Use a test builder pattern (factory functions like `makeCustomer`) to reduce boilerplate. Do NOT
suppress `?.`/`??` branches with `/* istanbul ignore next */` unless the null path is genuinely
unreachable at runtime — suppressing valid runtime branches hides real edge cases.

### Pattern 40 — Coverage for TypeScript async generators: ensuring all yield/return/throw paths are exercised  [community]

TypeScript async generators (`async function*`) produce complex coverage profiles because
Istanbul and V8 track multiple implicit branches: the `yield` path (iteration continues),
the `return` path (iteration completes), and the `throw` path (error during iteration).

```typescript
// src/streams/csv-parser.ts — async generator with multiple branch paths
export interface ParsedRow {
  index: number;
  fields: string[];
  isValid: boolean;
}

export class CsvParseError extends Error {
  constructor(public readonly lineIndex: number, cause: unknown) {
    super(`CSV parse error at line ${lineIndex}: ${String(cause)}`);
    this.name = 'CsvParseError';
  }
}

export async function* parseCsvLines(
  lines: AsyncIterable<string>,
  maxErrors: number = 5,
): AsyncGenerator<ParsedRow> {
  let index = 0;
  let errorCount = 0;
  for await (const line of lines) {
    index++;
    if (line.trim() === '') continue;  // branch: skip empty line
    try {
      const fields = line.split(',').map((f) => f.trim());
      const isValid = fields.every((f) => f.length > 0);
      yield { index, fields, isValid };    // branch: normal yield
    } catch (err) {
      errorCount++;
      if (errorCount > maxErrors) {
        throw new CsvParseError(index, err); // branch: throw path — too many errors
      }
      yield { index, fields: [], isValid: false }; // branch: error yield path
    }
  }
}
```

```typescript
// src/streams/csv-parser.test.ts — cover yield, return, throw, and continue branches
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { parseCsvLines, CsvParseError } from './csv-parser';

async function* fromArray(lines: string[]): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  for (const line of lines) yield line;
}

async function collect<T>(gen: AsyncGenerator<T>): Promise<T[]> {
  const results: T[] = [];
  for await (const item of gen) results.push(item);
  return results;
}

describe('parseCsvLines', () => {
  it('yields parsed rows for valid CSV lines (yield path)', async () => {
    const rows = await collect(parseCsvLines(fromArray(['a,b,c', 'd,e,f'])));
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(rows[0].fields).toEqual(['a', 'b', 'c']);
  });

  it('skips empty lines (continue branch)', async () => {
    const rows = await collect(parseCsvLines(fromArray(['a,b', '', 'c,d'])));
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it('completes iteration normally when all lines are valid (return path)', async () => {
    const rows = await collect(parseCsvLines(fromArray(['x,y'])));
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('yields invalid row on parse error within error limit (error yield path)', async () => {
    const rows = await collect(parseCsvLines(fromArray(['a,,c']), 3));
    expect(rows.some((r) => !r.isValid)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('throws CsvParseError when error count exceeds maxErrors (throw path)', async () => {
    async function* errorSource(): AsyncGenerator<string> {
      yield 'good,line';
      throw new Error('stream broken');
    }
    await expect(collect(parseCsvLines(errorSource(), 0))).rejects.toThrow(CsvParseError);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff**: async generator coverage requires explicit tests for each control-flow path:
normal yield, early continue/return, and throw propagation. The error/throw path is the most
commonly missed. Run Istanbul's HTML report and look for red markers on `throw` statements
inside catch blocks in async generators — these are the branches that need dedicated error-path
tests with mock-injected stream failures.

### Pattern 41 — Threshold drift detection: automated alert when coverage stagnates  [community]

Coverage thresholds set once rarely get raised. A module at 72 % branch coverage two years
ago may still be at 72 % today — the threshold was set, never updated. This pattern shows
how to generate a "coverage drift" alert that flags modules where coverage has not improved.

```typescript
// scripts/check-coverage-drift.ts — detect stagnating coverage via baseline comparison
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

interface FileCoverage {
  branches: { pct: number };
  lines: { pct: number };
}
interface CoverageSummary {
  total: FileCoverage;
  [file: string]: FileCoverage;
}

const BASELINE_PATH = resolve(process.cwd(), 'coverage/.coverage-baseline.json');
const SUMMARY_PATH = resolve(process.cwd(), 'coverage/coverage-summary.json');
const DRIFT_ALERT_THRESHOLD = -2; // alert if branch coverage dropped > 2% vs baseline

function checkCoverageDrift(): void {
  if (!existsSync(SUMMARY_PATH)) {
    console.log('No coverage-summary.json — run tests with coverage first.');
    process.exit(0);
  }

  const current: CoverageSummary = JSON.parse(readFileSync(SUMMARY_PATH, 'utf-8'));

  if (!existsSync(BASELINE_PATH)) {
    writeFileSync(BASELINE_PATH, JSON.stringify(current, null, 2));
    console.log('Coverage baseline created.');
    process.exit(0);
  }

  const baseline: CoverageSummary = JSON.parse(readFileSync(BASELINE_PATH, 'utf-8'));
  const drifted: string[] = [];

  for (const [filePath, currentEntry] of Object.entries(current)) {
    if (filePath === 'total') continue;
    const baseEntry = baseline[filePath];
    if (!baseEntry) continue;
    const drift = currentEntry.branches.pct - baseEntry.branches.pct;
    if (drift < DRIFT_ALERT_THRESHOLD) {
      drifted.push(
        `${filePath}: branch coverage drifted ${baseEntry.branches.pct.toFixed(1)}% → ` +
        `${currentEntry.branches.pct.toFixed(1)}% (Δ ${drift.toFixed(1)}%)`,
      );
    }
  }

  if (drifted.length > 0) {
    console.error(`Coverage drift in ${drifted.length} file(s):\n` + drifted.join('\n'));
    process.exitCode = 1;
  } else {
    console.log('No coverage drift detected.');
    writeFileSync(BASELINE_PATH, JSON.stringify(current, null, 2));
  }
}

checkCoverageDrift();
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/coverage-drift.yml — weekly drift alert
name: Coverage Drift Alert
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 9 * * 1'  # every Monday 09:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  drift-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx vitest run --coverage --coverage.reporter=json-summary
      - run: npx tsx scripts/check-coverage-drift.ts
```

**Tradeoff**: baseline files must be committed or stored as CI artifacts. Committing is simpler
but adds noise to the git log. This pattern is most useful for teams using `autoUpdate: false`
who want an automated reminder that coverage has not improved after several sprints. Do NOT use
as a hard PR gate — drift can occur legitimately after refactors that change baselines.

### Pattern 42 — ESM dual-package coverage: verifying source coverage across CJS and ESM builds  [community]

Libraries shipping both CJS and ESM builds need coverage collected from the source TypeScript
rather than the compiled output to keep HTML reports readable. The key is ensuring both
build outputs are excluded from `coverage.include` while source is fully covered.

```typescript
// src/lib/number-utils.ts — utility library with dual build
export function roundHalfEven(value: number, decimals: number): number {
  // Banker's rounding: rounds 0.5 to the nearest even number (IEEE 754 standard).
  if (decimals < 0) throw new RangeError(`decimals must be >= 0, got ${decimals}`);
  const factor = Math.pow(10, decimals);
  const shifted = value * factor;
  const floor = Math.floor(shifted);
  const diff = shifted - floor;
  if (diff === 0.5) {
    // Round to nearest even: if floor is odd, round up; if even, round down.
    return (floor % 2 === 0 ? floor : floor + 1) / factor;
  }
  return Math.round(shifted) / factor;
}
```

```typescript
// tests/number-utils.test.ts — covers all branches of roundHalfEven
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { roundHalfEven } from '../src/lib/number-utils';

describe('roundHalfEven', () => {
  it('rounds 0.5 down to 0 (nearest even, floor is 0 which is even)', () => {
    expect(roundHalfEven(0.5, 0)).toBe(0);
  });
  it('rounds 1.5 up to 2 (nearest even, floor is 1 which is odd)', () => {
    expect(roundHalfEven(1.5, 0)).toBe(2);
  });
  it('rounds 2.5 down to 2 (nearest even, floor is 2 which is even)', () => {
    expect(roundHalfEven(2.5, 0)).toBe(2);
  });
  it('rounds non-halves using standard rounding (diff !== 0.5 branch)', () => {
    expect(roundHalfEven(1.4, 0)).toBe(1);
    expect(roundHalfEven(1.6, 0)).toBe(2);
  });
  it('throws on negative decimals (RangeError branch)', () => {
    expect(() => roundHalfEven(1.5, -1)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
  it('handles multi-decimal rounding', () => {
    expect(roundHalfEven(1.555, 2)).toBeCloseTo(1.56, 2);
  });
});
```

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — dual-package library: collect coverage only from source TypeScript
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      // Only source TypeScript — NOT the compiled dist/ directories.
      include: ['src/**/*.ts'],
      exclude: [
        'src/**/*.d.ts',
        'src/**/*.test.ts',
        'dist/**',         // CJS build — do NOT instrument
        'dist-esm/**',     // ESM build — do NOT instrument
      ],
      all: true,
      reporter: ['text', 'html', 'lcov', 'json-summary'],
      thresholds: { lines: 90, branches: 85, functions: 90, statements: 90 },
    },
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff**: collecting coverage on TypeScript source (with source maps) during development
keeps HTML reports readable. Always exclude `dist/` and `dist-esm/` from `coverage.include` —
if the compiled output is accidentally included, you will see duplicate coverage entries and
inflated numbers. Use `excludeAfterRemap: true` (G39) to prevent compiler helpers from
polluting source-level reports.

### Pattern 43 — Coverage badge generation from `coverage-summary.json`  [community]

Automating coverage badge generation from `coverage-summary.json` provides a visible quality
signal in the repository README without requiring Codecov or Shields.io.

```typescript
// scripts/generate-coverage-badge.ts — SVG badge from coverage-summary.json
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

interface CoverageSummary {
  total: {
    lines: { pct: number };
    branches: { pct: number };
    functions: { pct: number };
    statements: { pct: number };
  };
}

function getBadgeColor(pct: number): string {
  if (pct >= 90) return '#4c1';
  if (pct >= 80) return '#97ca00';
  if (pct >= 70) return '#dfb317';
  if (pct >= 50) return '#fe7d37';
  return '#e05d44';
}

function generateSvgBadge(label: string, value: string, color: string): string {
  const lw = label.length * 6 + 10;
  const vw = value.length * 6 + 10;
  const tw = lw + vw;
  return `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${tw}" height="20">` +
    `<rect width="${lw}" height="20" fill="#555"/>` +
    `<rect x="${lw}" width="${vw}" height="20" fill="${color}"/>` +
    `<text x="${lw / 2}" y="14" fill="#fff" font-size="11" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">${label}</text>` +
    `<text x="${lw + vw / 2}" y="14" fill="#fff" font-size="11" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">${value}</text>` +
    `</svg>`;
}

function main(): void {
  const summaryPath = resolve(process.cwd(), 'coverage/coverage-summary.json');
  const summary: CoverageSummary = JSON.parse(readFileSync(summaryPath, 'utf-8'));
  const branchPct = summary.total.branches.pct;
  const linePct = summary.total.lines.pct;

  writeFileSync(
    resolve(process.cwd(), 'coverage/branch-coverage.svg'),
    generateSvgBadge('branches', `${branchPct.toFixed(0)}%`, getBadgeColor(branchPct)),
  );
  writeFileSync(
    resolve(process.cwd(), 'coverage/coverage.svg'),
    generateSvgBadge('coverage', `${linePct.toFixed(0)}%`, getBadgeColor(linePct)),
  );
  console.log(`Branch: ${branchPct.toFixed(1)}%, Lines: ${linePct.toFixed(1)}%`);
}

main();
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/coverage-badge.yml — commit badge after main push
name: Coverage Badge
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  badge:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx vitest run --coverage --coverage.reporter=json-summary
      - run: npx tsx scripts/generate-coverage-badge.ts
      - name: Commit updated badge
        run: |
          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
          git config user.email 'github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git add coverage/coverage.svg coverage/branch-coverage.svg
          git diff --staged --quiet || git commit -m 'chore: update coverage badges'
          git push
```

**Tradeoff**: self-hosted badge generation avoids Codecov/Shields.io dependencies. The downside
is that badge SVGs are committed on every push to main. Alternative: write badge SVG to
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` as HTML inline rather than committing — no git history noise.

### Pattern 44 — Functional coverage vs structural coverage: mapping acceptance criteria to test cases  [community]

Structural coverage (line, branch, mutation) measures what the code does when executed.
Functional coverage measures whether each **requirement** or **acceptance criterion** has at
least one test. High structural coverage does not guarantee functional coverage.

```typescript
// src/domain/subscription-engine.ts — business rules with explicit AC mapping
export type Plan = 'free' | 'pro' | 'enterprise';

const ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS: Record<Plan, Plan[]> = {
  free: ['pro', 'enterprise'],
  pro: ['free', 'enterprise'],
  enterprise: ['pro'],   // enterprise cannot downgrade to free per business rule
};

export interface SubscriptionTransition {
  from: Plan;
  to: Plan;
  allowedAt: Date;
  reason: string;
}

export function validateTransition(
  from: Plan,
  to: Plan,
  requestedAt: Date,
): SubscriptionTransition | null {
  const allowed = ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[from];
  if (!allowed.includes(to)) return null;

  // Enforce 30-day cooldown on downgrades from paid plans:
  const isDowngrade = from === 'enterprise' || (from === 'pro' && to === 'free');
  const daysSince = (requestedAt.getTime() - Date.now()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
  if (isDowngrade && daysSince > -30) return null;

  return { from, to, allowedAt: requestedAt, reason: 'Validated' };
}
```

```typescript
// src/domain/subscription-engine.test.ts — AC-tagged tests for requirement traceability
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { validateTransition } from './subscription-engine';

const NOW = new Date();
const PAST_31_DAYS = new Date(Date.now() - 31 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);

describe('validateTransition — plan change rules', () => {
  // AC-1: Free users can upgrade to Pro
  it('[AC-1] free → pro upgrade is allowed', () => {
    expect(validateTransition('free', 'pro', NOW)).not.toBeNull();
  });

  // AC-2: Free users can upgrade directly to Enterprise
  it('[AC-2] free → enterprise upgrade is allowed', () => {
    expect(validateTransition('free', 'enterprise', NOW)).not.toBeNull();
  });

  // AC-3: Enterprise cannot downgrade to Free at all (forbidden transition)
  it('[AC-3] enterprise → free is never allowed', () => {
    expect(validateTransition('enterprise', 'free', NOW)).toBeNull();
  });

  // AC-4: Enterprise can downgrade to Pro after 30-day cooldown
  it('[AC-4] enterprise → pro allowed after 30-day cooldown', () => {
    expect(validateTransition('enterprise', 'pro', PAST_31_DAYS)).not.toBeNull();
  });

  // AC-5: Pro cannot downgrade to Free within 30-day cooldown window
  it('[AC-5] pro → free is blocked within 30-day cooldown', () => {
    expect(validateTransition('pro', 'free', NOW)).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff**: requirement-mapped test names with AC tags make failing tests immediately point
to the broken requirement — triage is faster. Reserve AC-tagged tests for business-rule
functions where requirements are formally documented. Infrastructure and utility code benefits
more from property-based testing than from requirement tracing. Do NOT AC-tag every unit test
— the overhead is justified only when requirements are tracked in a backlog or spec document.

### Pattern 45 — Custom post-run coverage notification via `coverage-summary.json`  [community]

Istanbul's coverage reporter API allows writing custom reporters that fire on coverage
completion. A lightweight alternative is to read `coverage-summary.json` post-run and
send a webhook notification when branch coverage drops below threshold.

```typescript
// scripts/notify-coverage-drop.ts — Slack notification on coverage drop
import { readFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

interface CoverageSummary {
  total: { branches: { pct: number }; lines: { pct: number }; functions: { pct: number } };
}

async function notifySlack(webhookUrl: string, branchPct: number, repo: string): Promise<void> {
  const emoji = branchPct >= 75 ? ':white_check_mark:' : ':warning:';
  await fetch(webhookUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      blocks: [
        {
          type: 'section',
          text: {
            type: 'mrkdwn',
            text: `${emoji} *Coverage Drop* in \`${repo}\`\nBranch coverage: *${branchPct.toFixed(1)}%* (threshold: 75%)`,
          },
        },
      ],
    }),
  });
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const summaryPath = resolve(process.cwd(), 'coverage/coverage-summary.json');
  if (!existsSync(summaryPath)) return;

  const summary: CoverageSummary = JSON.parse(readFileSync(summaryPath, 'utf-8'));
  const branchPct = summary.total.branches.pct;
  const webhookUrl = process.env.SLACK_COVERAGE_WEBHOOK;

  if (!webhookUrl) {
    console.log('SLACK_COVERAGE_WEBHOOK not set — skipping notification.');
    return;
  }

  const THRESHOLD = 75;
  if (branchPct < THRESHOLD) {
    const repo = process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY ?? 'unknown-repo';
    await notifySlack(webhookUrl, branchPct, repo);
    console.log(`Notified Slack: branch coverage at ${branchPct.toFixed(1)}%`);
  } else {
    console.log(`Branch coverage ${branchPct.toFixed(1)}% is above threshold — no notification sent.`);
  }
}

main().catch(console.error);
```

**Tradeoff**: webhook notifications add external dependencies and secret management overhead.
Gate the notification on a threshold drop to prevent alert fatigue. Do NOT fire on every
coverage run. For teams already using Codecov or SonarCloud, their native Slack integrations
are more featureful and require no custom code — this pattern is best for teams without
external coverage services who want simple team awareness.

### Pattern 46 — React custom hooks: targeted branch coverage with `renderHook`  [community]

React custom hooks contain branching logic (loading states, error states, conditional effects)
that is frequently undertested because hook tests require the `renderHook` wrapper. Teams
testing only components often have zero branch coverage on hooks used inside those components.

```typescript
// src/hooks/use-async-data.ts — custom hook with loading/error/success branches
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

export type AsyncState<T> =
  | { status: 'idle' }
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { status: 'success'; data: T }
  | { status: 'error'; error: Error };

export function useAsyncData<T>(
  fetcher: (() => Promise<T>) | null,
): AsyncState<T> {
  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'idle' });

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!fetcher) return;    // branch: no fetcher (idle path)

    let cancelled = false;
    setState({ status: 'loading' });

    fetcher()
      .then((data) => {
        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'success', data });  // branch: success
      })
      .catch((err: Error) => {
        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'error', error: err });  // branch: error
      });

    return () => { cancelled = true; };   // branch: cleanup on unmount
  }, [fetcher]);

  return state;
}
```

```typescript
// src/hooks/use-async-data.test.ts — renderHook tests for branch coverage
import { renderHook, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import { vi, describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { useAsyncData } from './use-async-data';

describe('useAsyncData', () => {
  it('stays idle when fetcher is null (no-fetcher branch)', () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useAsyncData(null));
    expect(result.current.status).toBe('idle');
  });

  it('transitions to loading then success (loading + success branches)', async () => {
    const fetcher = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ id: 1, name: 'Alice' });
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useAsyncData(fetcher));
    expect(result.current.status).toBe('loading');
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.status).toBe('success'));
    if (result.current.status === 'success') {
      expect(result.current.data).toEqual({ id: 1, name: 'Alice' });
    }
  });

  it('transitions to error state when fetcher rejects (error branch)', async () => {
    const fetcher = vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('Network error'));
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useAsyncData(fetcher));
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.status).toBe('error'));
    if (result.current.status === 'error') {
      expect(result.current.error.message).toBe('Network error');
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff**: `renderHook` tests require `@testing-library/react` and a DOM environment
(`environment: 'jsdom'` in Vitest config). They are the only reliable way to achieve meaningful
branch coverage on hooks that use `useEffect`, `useState`, and async state transitions. Do NOT
test hooks exclusively through component tests — the component's render tree often masks the
hook's internal branching logic.

### Pattern 47 — Vitest `coverage.include` with TypeScript project references: cross-package source coverage  [community]

TypeScript composite builds (`references` in `tsconfig.json`) allow packages to reference
each other without `node_modules`. Vitest's `coverage.include` does not automatically follow
project references — cross-package source files must be explicitly listed.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — composite TypeScript project references coverage
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: {
    // TypeScript composite project references resolved as source paths:
    alias: {
      '@shared': resolve(__dirname, '../shared/src'),
      '@validation': resolve(__dirname, '../validation/src'),
    },
  },
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      // Include source from this package AND referenced packages:
      include: [
        'src/**/*.ts',
        '../shared/src/**/*.ts',
        '../validation/src/**/*.ts',
      ],
      exclude: [
        '**/*.d.ts',
        '**/*.test.ts',
        '**/*.spec.ts',
        '**/__mocks__/**',
        '**/index.ts',
      ],
      // allowExternal: true is required for files outside the project root:
      allowExternal: true,
      reporter: ['text', 'html', 'lcov', 'json-summary'],
      reportsDirectory: './coverage',
      thresholds: {
        lines: 80,
        branches: 75,
        functions: 80,
        statements: 80,
      },
    },
  },
});
```

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "composite": true,
    "sourceMap": true,
    "declarationMap": true,
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "outDir": "./dist"
  },
  "references": [
    { "path": "../shared" },
    { "path": "../validation" }
  ],
  "include": ["src/**/*.ts"]
}
```

**Tradeoff**: `allowExternal: true` with explicit `include` paths gives accurate cross-package
coverage but requires manual maintenance — adding a new referenced package means updating both
`tsconfig.json` references and `vitest.config.ts` `include` arrays. Always pair `allowExternal: true`
with narrow explicit `include` patterns to avoid collecting coverage for `node_modules`. Consider
running per-package coverage in CI and aggregating with LCOV merge tools as an alternative.
